answer:
Headline results for run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (read-only report; no PBS jobs, no hazard.py):

Records analysed: 759 (stride 20), spanning 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z (3.314% of the time window).
Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57.
DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above Mc).

Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days.
Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016).

CALIBRATED probabilities (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — this is the calibrated one):
  b=1.0:  Sigma = -5.449, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.0001198, P(M>=5.5) over observed volume = 5.236e-06, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.03719
  b=0.73: Sigma = -5.319, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.004922,  P(M>=5.5) over observed volume = 0.0002155, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.2809
  b=0.65: Sigma = -5.281, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.01474,   P(M>=5.5) over observed volume = 0.0006484, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.4653

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts — this is the upper bound, not the calibrated estimate):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated LBNL-catalogue-based probabilities indicate a very low annual likelihood of a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event (1.2e-4 to 1.5e-2 per year depending on the b scenario), while the DAS-based upper bound (0.078 per year at b=0.9849) is higher because uncalibrated DAS magnitudes cause every detection to be counted as an event at or above Mc, over-counting the seismicity rate.
